paper_diagnosis: Primary toxoplasmosis infection in a kidney-transplant patient complicated by acute left-ventricular failure
disease_label_per_paper: Primary toxoplasmosis after kidney transplantation with hemophagocytic syndrome, hemolytic anemia, and probable toxoplasmosis-induced myocarditis/left ventricular failure
presentation_summary: Male kidney transplant recipient born in 1982 with chronic allograft nephropathy was taking tacrolimus, mycophenolate mofetil, and prednisolone when he developed daily hyperthermia above 39 C.
He presented with maculopapular skin eruptions, diarrhea, vomiting, and 10% weight loss over 2 weeks.
Admission exam showed temperature 39 C, blood pressure 150/85 mmHg, heart rate 100 bpm, and no edema.
Labs showed severe renal failure, hemolytic anemia, very high LDH, thrombocytopenia, leukopenia/neutropenia, and bone marrow features of hemophagocytic syndrome.

Blood and bone-marrow PCR confirmed T. gondii and serology converted to IgM positive without IgG; six weeks into therapy he developed severe dyspnea, tachycardia, hypotension, and left ventricular ejection fraction around 10%.
He improved after adding sulfamethoxazole/trimethoprim and heart-failure therapy, with ejection fraction recovering to 47% within about two months and later 60%.

actual_treatment: daily hemodialysis then three times weekly dialysis
tacrolimus and mycophenolate stopped; prednisolone continued
sulfamethoxazole/trimethoprim 800/120 mg after each dialysis session added after left ventricular failure
ramipril, digoxin, bisoprolol, and spironolactone for heart failure

outcome.source_text_value: The ejection fraction further increased to 60% by October 2002 ... More than 3 years after his third kidney transplantation no toxoplasmosis reactivation occurred
